cards.explanation: The answer is that his little daughter is near death. Jairus, a synagogue leader, puts it plainly: “My little daughter is near death.” That's why he's down at Jesus' feet, pleading urgently. I think a man in that spot has stopped caring who's watching. He just wants Jesus to come.

The answer is True. Jairus says, “Please come and place Your hands on her, so that she will be healed and live.” He asks for two things in one breath: that Jesus come, and that she live. Notice he doesn't ask for a speech or a plan. He asks Jesus to come.

The answer is False. She didn't get better. She spent all she had on many physicians, and the text says, “…her condition had only grown worse.” That's a heavy part of her story, friends. I think it's why what comes next hits so hard.
The answer is that she touches His cloak. Mark 5:27 says she came up through the crowd behind Him and touched His cloak. That's what she does, and nothing more is said about how.

The answer is healed. She kept saying, “If only I touch His garments, I will be healed.” That's her own sentence from Mark 5:28. She wasn't just thinking it once, either, bakers. The text says she kept saying it.

The answer is that it stops immediately. Mark 5:29 says, “Immediately her bleeding stopped…” No waiting and no slow improvement. She also sensed in her body that she was healed, right there in the crowd.

The answer is “Who touched My garments?” Jesus is aware that power has gone out from Him, and He turns to the crowd to ask. His question is about a touch. Out of all those people pressing in, one touch was different.

The answer is False. The disciples don't point her out. Mark 5:31 has them say, “You can see the crowd pressing in on You, and yet You ask, ‘Who touched Me?’…” Their answer is about the crowd pressing in. It names no one.
The answer is False. Jesus doesn't drop it. The text says, “But He kept looking around to see who had done this.” The disciples gave their answer, friends, and Jesus kept looking around the crowd.
The answer is the whole truth. Mark 5:33 says she came, fell down before Him trembling in fear, and “…told Him the whole truth.” She doesn't leave anything out. I think that took real nerve.

The answer is False. There's no scolding. Mark 5:34 has Jesus say, “Daughter,” and then, “your faith has healed you. Go in peace and be free of your affliction.” She came in fear, and He sent her off with those words.

The answer is faith. Jesus says, “Daughter,” and then, “your faith has healed you.” That's Mark 5:34. He names her faith out loud, right in front of the crowd. Then He sends her off in peace, free of her affliction.

The answer is that his daughter is dead. The messengers say it straight: “Your daughter is dead…” That's Mark 5:35, and it lands on Jairus while Jesus is still speaking to the woman. This is a heavy moment, and I think Jairus feels every word of it.

The answer is that Jesus tells him not to be afraid but just believe. Jesus overheard them and said to Jairus, “Do not be afraid; just believe.” That's Mark 5:36. He speaks right to Jairus the moment the bad news lands. Short words for a heavy moment.

The answer is False. There's no crowd. Mark 5:37 says He did not allow anyone to accompany Him except Peter, James, and John the brother of James. Just three of His disciples go with Him to the house.

The answer is that she is not dead but asleep. Jesus says, “The child is not dead, but asleep.” That's Mark 5:39, spoken right into all that weeping and wailing. He asks them first, “Why all this commotion and weeping?” Then He tells them what He says about the girl.

The answer is laughed. Mark 5:40 says, “And they laughed at Him.” Jesus had just said the child was not dead but asleep, and the people there laughed. It's a sad kind of laughter, I think, from people in the middle of grief.
The answer is False. Not everyone stays. Mark 5:40 says Jesus put them all outside. Then He took the child's father and mother and His own companions, and went in to see the child.

The answer is “Little girl, I say to you, get up!” Mark 5:41 gives us the words and the meaning right together: “Talitha koum!” which means, “Little girl, I say to you, get up!” Jesus takes her by the hand and speaks directly to her. The writer even stops to translate it for us.
The answer is True. Mark 5:42 says, “Immediately the girl got up and began to walk around…” Jesus says get up, and she gets up. Right away, friends, she's walking around.

The answer is twelve. The writer tells us, “…(she was twelve years old).” That's Mark 5:42, tucked in right as she starts walking around. Twelve also showed up earlier for the woman's years of bleeding, in Mark 5:25. Same number, two different stories running side by side.

The answer is to give her something to eat. Mark 5:43 says Jesus “…told them to give her something to eat.” After all that astonishment, there's a plain, practical instruction. I think it's a good reminder that even after a miracle, a hungry person still needs a meal.
